title: Cheese and Onion Pasties
subtitle: Flaky shortcrust pastry filled with cheese, raw potato and onion
excerpt: These hand-crimped pasties are filled with raw potato, onion and cheddar that cook together inside the pastry. They are simple, satisfying and very British.
sourceNotes: Pasties are most closely associated with Cornwall, where they were traditionally filled with meat and root vegetables. Cheese and onion is a popular vegetarian variation across Britain.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked. Place on a tray to freeze, then transfer to bags. Bake from frozen at 200C for 45 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: The recipe doubles well. Make the pastry in two batches for best texture.

content.text: The potato goes in raw. It steams inside the pastry and cooks through during baking.
Preheat your oven to 200C. Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Put the flour in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Add the cold butter.
Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Add 4 to 5 tablespoons of cold water, a little at a time. Mix until the dough just comes together.
Divide the dough into 6 equal balls. Roll each one to a circle about 20cm across.
Mix the potato, onion and cheddar in a bowl. Season well with salt and pepper. Add mustard if using.
Pile the filling on one half of each circle, leaving a 2cm border.
Brush the border with egg wash. Fold the pastry over and press the edges firmly.
Crimp the edge by folding and pressing with your fingers or a fork.
Brush all over with egg wash. Cut a small steam hole in the top.
Bake for 35 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes before eating.

items.cause: Slices were too thick or bake was too short.
items.fix: Slice the potato as thin as possible next time.

items.cause: The filling was overfilled or the steam hole was blocked.
items.fix: Fill less generously and make the steam hole bigger.

items.cause: Tray was not hot enough or oven was too low.
items.fix: Use the bottom shelf and check the oven temperature.
